title: simpleNMR /simpleMNOVA input JSON contract
description: Structural definition of the JSON file submitted by MNova, Bruker, and JEOL/JASON client converters to simpleNMRtools' /simpleMNOVA endpoint. Generated from simpleNMR_field_manifest.yaml — every constraint here traces back to a confirmed finding in that manifest, not assumption. Fields the manifest marked 'required: unknown' are deliberately left OPTIONAL in this schema rather than omitted or required, per an explicit decision to tighten only as each is confirmed. This schema validates STRUCTURE and TYPE only; the one hard cross-field business rule (HSQC must actually be present and not SKIP'd) cannot be expressed in JSON Schema alone and is checked separately by validate_simplenmr_json.py.

envelope_singleton_scalar.description: category: singleton_scalar — parsed server-side via DataFrame(data, index=[0]).

data.description: Single-value payload keyed by the string '0'.

envelope_indexed_dict.description: category: indexed_dict — parsed server-side via DataFrame.from_dict(data, orient='index'). Each record in 'data' is validated against atomInfoRecord for the fields that apply (atom_idx, atomNumber, numProtons) — extra source-specific columns per record are permitted, since allAtomsInfo/carbonAtomsInfo/nmrAssignments/c13predictions each carry a different real column set per the manifest.

data.description: Dict of records, keyed by string row index.

envelope_special_string_list.description: category: special — chosenSpectra / exptIdentifiers / spectraWithPeaks shape: dict of string-indexed values.

atomInfoRecord.description: One record inside allAtomsInfo / carbonAtomsInfo / nmrAssignments / c13predictions. atomNumber is a free-form user-facing DISPLAY LABEL (supports primed forms like "4'", "6''") and is NOT the same as atom_idx, which is the true molfile/RDKit structural index — confirmed real example: atomNumber "6'" alongside a purely numeric atom_idx on the same record.

atomNumber.description: Free-form display label. May be numeric-looking (server coerces numeric strings to int for display) or an arbitrary string such as a primed label. Typed as a string here since that is its true semantic type; numeric JSON values are also accepted since some sources (e.g. JEOL/JASON) submit it as int.

smiles.description: required: everywhere. No graceful server-side fallback if absent — NMRProblem.add_missing_spectra does not cover this key, and nmrsolution.py accesses it via unguarded dict indexing. Validate presence carefully at the interface layer.

molfile.description: required: everywhere. Same no-graceful-fallback caveat as smiles.

hostname.description: required: everywhere — confirmed for all three sources (Bruker, JEOL by code reading; MNova by direct confirmation and a real submitted file). Mac-based device id, used server-side for device registration/licensing gating. Degrades gracefully if missing (extract_hostname() returns "" on KeyError), unlike smiles/molfile/carbonAtomsInfo.

carbonAtomsInfo.description: required: everywhere. Minimally needs atom_idx and atomNumber per record — other columns (ppm, x, y, iupacLabel, jCouplingVals/Class, H1_ppm, visible) are server-computed/overwritten, not trusted input. No graceful fallback if the key itself is missing — same caveat as smiles/molfile.

nmrAssignments.description: required: [mnova, bruker], missing_from: [jason] — left optional here since not universal. Minimally needs atom_idx, atomNumber, f1_ppm, f2_ppm1, f2_ppm2 per record (f2_ppm3 present in real files but confirmed unused server-side).

c13predictions.description: required: conditional — legitimately empty/absent when no carbon-shift predictor is available for that source. Only trusted server-side when MNOVAcalcMethod is 'JEOL Predict' or 'MNOVA Predict' (JEOL_prediction_used() gate) — for 'NMRSHIFTDB2 Predict' or any other value the server recomputes its own shifts and ignores this field even if present.

MNOVAcalcMethod.description: required: everywhere. Observed values: 'MNOVA Predict', 'NMRSHIFTDB2 Predict', 'JEOL Predict', or other/empty. Gates three server-side methods (is_prediction, prediction_from_nmrshiftdb2, JEOL_prediction_used) with confirmed non-obvious behavior — see manifest for the c13predictions trust-logic correction.

carbonCalcPositionsMethod.description: required: [jason, bruker], missing_from: [mnova] — left optional here.

workingDirectory.description: required: unknown — left optional pending confirmation. Confirmed server_consumed: false (passthrough) in core, but used by Bruker's own client for saving the HTML response locally.

workingFilename.description: required: unknown — left optional pending confirmation. Same passthrough/client-local-use pattern as workingDirectory.

simulatedAnnealing.description: required: everywhere (corrected from an earlier bruker-only read — confirmed present in MNova's real payload too). Boolean on/off flag; the ONLY simulated-annealing field that should be part of the contract going forward. Real solve additionally requires simAnneal.predicted_weight > 0 server-side, invisible from the input JSON.

ml_consent.description: required: everywhere. Boolean. Falls back to False on KeyError server-side, so effectively optional in practice despite being read unconditionally — included as required here since it is always actually submitted in real files from all three sources.

randomizeStart.description: DEPRECATED FROM CONTRACT — may still appear as passthrough (particularly MNova). Not required; presence, absence, or cross-source inconsistency should not be flagged as an error by any diff/golden-file tooling built on this schema.

coolingRate.description: DEPRECATED FROM CONTRACT — see randomizeStart. Also independently confirmed unused server-side (a hardcoded constant is used instead).

chosenSpectra.description: required: everywhere — confirmed for all three sources. Each string value ends in the chosen experiment type as its final whitespace-delimited token (server parses via s.split()[-1]); the literal token 'SKIP' as that final token is valid and expected to be stripped server-side. MNova submits SKIP'd spectra with the literal token present; Bruker and JEOL both intend to filter SKIP'd spectra out before submission entirely (JEOL's filtering has a confirmed bug that can let some through — see manifest). Either pattern is accepted by the server; a schema/converter should not assume only one is correct.

exptIdentifiers.description: required: [mnova, bruker], missing_from: [jason] confirmed by direct code reading — left optional here. Distinct SKIP semantics from chosenSpectra depending on source: for MNova it mirrors the user's full per-spectrum dropdown assignment (including SKIP as an explicit choice); for Bruker it is built from ALL raw detected experiments (not just user-selected ones) with 'SKIP' as a fallback meaning 'auto-classifier could not identify this experiment type' — a different meaning from the same string elsewhere.

spectraWithPeaks.description: required: unknown — left optional pending confirmation.

subtype.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

pulsesequence.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

intrument.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough; sic, typo preserved from the source field name).

probe.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

class.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

origin.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

spectype.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

experiment.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

filename.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

datafilename.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

expt_fn.description: required: unknown, server_consumed: false (passthrough, per-spectrum-block metadata).

^(H1_1D|C13_1D|DEPT135|HSQC|HMBC|COSY|NO.description: Spectrum-block field (category: spectrum_block). Multiple blocks of the SAME experiment type (e.g. HSQC_0 + HSQC_1) are an intentional, supported workflow for ANY of the 10 NMREXPERIMENTS types, confirmed by Eric — e.g. two acquisitions of the same experiment collected under different regimes for improved resolution. The server combines same-type blocks into one dataframe via exact-value ppm de-duplication (no tolerance window — see manifest's caution_exact_match_dedup for a flagged-but-unconfirmed concern about whether this achieves true reconciliation across different-resolution acquisitions). A key literally prefixed 'SKIP' (e.g. 'SKIP_0') is valid and expected: MNova tags a user-skipped spectrum's own block with the dropdown value as its classification prefix, which independently guarantees it can never classify into a real experiment type regardless of chosenSpectra string parsing. NOESY classifies and parses like any other type but is confirmed never read by any server-side solving logic — a legitimate but functionally inert passthrough.

type.description: '1D' or '2D' — this, not the key name, is what the server actually uses to decide 1D vs 2D parsing.

nucleus.description: server_consumed: false (passthrough). Type varies by source in real files — harmless since unconsumed.

experimenttype.description: server_consumed: false (passthrough) — vocabulary differs across sources, confirmed harmless since not used for classification.
